documents.body: Prime Minister Aleksander Norvik today delivered the annual defence budget statement to Veridia’s parliament, outlining planned spending for the next fiscal year. Norvik reaffirmed the government's commitment to maintaining defence expenditure at 2.7% of Gross Domestic Product, a target set three years ago. The budget prioritizes modernization of the Veridian Coastal Guard and increased investment in cyber security infrastructure. Opposition members questioned the allocation of funds toward personnel training, suggesting a potential skills shortage within the armed forces.

documents.title: Prime Minister Norvik Opens Verithall-Stamvik High-Speed Rail
documents.body: Prime Minister Aleksander Norvik officially inaugurated the new Verithall to Stamvik high-speed rail line today at a ceremony held at Verithall Central station. The 180-kilometer line, completed six months ahead of schedule, will significantly reduce travel time between the two cities, cutting it from three hours to just 90 minutes. Norvik hailed the project as a pivotal moment for Veridia’s infrastructure and economic development, emphasizing its potential to connect communities and boost regional growth. The first commercial trains are scheduled to depart tomorrow morning.

Discussions are centered around revised financial incentives and enhanced operational cooperation to curb irregular crossings towards Europe. Several ministers are expected to voice reservations regarding the enforceability of commitments from partner nations.

documents.body: Europe’s scrambling to outsource its border control to unstable North African nations, and the latest EU meeting signals a worrying escalation of that trend. While financial sweeteners and promises of cooperation sound nice, the reality is that relying on Tunisia and Libya to manage migration flows is a deeply flawed and likely unsustainable strategy. Expecting these governments to reliably uphold their commitments, given their own internal challenges, feels naive at best and exploitative at worst. Ultimately, this approach simply pushes the problem further out to sea, with potentially devastating consequences for vulnerable people.
